items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: And actually you know they had Buddy Rich on the show? ... And then Buddy’s looking at him and he says, “who’s this?” ... I love that thing.

ctx.x: And you guys would be in the pit?

Yeah we would be in the pit, and they’d have orchestrations, and we just played background music. It was nothing really serious, but it was soft. Because they had to hear the explosions, talking about the way they used to blow each other away when they were new. It’s so funny, unbelievable. And they grew up to be such an empire that I was a very, very big admirer of Animal, of course. And actually you know they had Buddy Rich on the show?

items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: And then at the end the dialogue is they bring Animal... He says, 'that's Animal.'

ctx.x: When he played the room? And he played the stage and stuff.

And walks down and plays all over the stage. And then at the end the dialogue is they bring Animal, “kill, kill, kill, drum battle, drum battle, kill.” And Buddy’s looking at him and he says, “who’s this?” He says, “that’s Animal.” He says, “he looks like an animal.” He says, “if he breaks his chain you’ll look like an animal.” So anyway it was fantastic. So they get up there and they play back and forth, and Ronnie Verrell was the drummer, an English drummer for the group in the band in London, and he was a…
Yeah. You have a copy of that you said?
